meta.name: Review contract clauses against your playbook with Google Drive and Claude

name: Contract review against your playbook, clause by clause, with a reviewer decision gate

parameters.content:
## Contract review against your playbook, clause by clause, with a reviewer decision gate

### How it works

This workflow reviews uploaded contracts clause by clause against a configured legal playbook. It can start from a Google Drive upload or a manual run, downloads and encodes the contract, uses Claude to extract clauses, then loops through each clause with an AI assessment agent. After aggregating the findings, it either auto-clears the contract or routes it to a reviewer decision gate before producing a report, logging the review, and sending a completion notice.

### Setup steps

- Configure Google Drive credentials for the upload trigger and file download node, including the watched folder or file source.
- Set the review configuration values such as ourSide, playbook, hardLimits, anthropicModel, reviewer channel/webhook URL, and completion notification endpoint.
- Configure Anthropic credentials/API headers for the Claude HTTP request and the Claude model used by the AI Agent.
- Configure Google Sheets credentials and select the target spreadsheet/table for the review log.
- Ensure the reviewer decision wait/resume URL or approval mechanism matches the payload posted to the reviewer channel.

### Customization

Update the playbook, hard limits, clause extraction prompt, assessment schema, escalation rules, reviewer message format, and ledger columns to match the organization’s contract review policy.

## Start and load contract

Handles the two workflow entry paths, applies manual review configuration, and downloads the contract file from Google Drive.

## Prepare extraction payload

Converts the downloaded contract into Base64 and builds the request body needed for clause extraction.

## Extract contract clauses

Calls Claude to identify clauses in the contract and parses the returned clause list for downstream processing.

## Assess clauses iteratively

Loops through extracted clauses, assesses each one against the playbook using an AI Agent and Claude model, validates the structured schema, and captures each assessment before continuing the loop.

## Aggregate and decide

Collects all clause-level findings after the loop completes and determines whether the review requires escalation.

## Auto-clear branch

Marks the review as auto-cleared when no escalation is required, preparing it for final report generation.

## Reviewer decision gate

Builds the escalation message, posts it to the reviewer channel, waits for the reviewer’s response, and records the final human decision.

## Build final records

Creates the final review report and converts it into a structured ledger row for persistence.

## Log review outcome

Appends the completed review record to the configured Google Sheets review log.

## Send completion notice

Posts a completion notification after the review has been logged.

nodes.name: When Contract Uploaded
nodes.notes: Point at the folder where contracts for review are dropped.

nodes.name: Configure Review Settings
nodes.notes: playbook and hardLimits are read into the assessment prompt verbatim. Hard limits are checked deterministically afterwards, so write them as things you would actually walk away over.

assignments.name: ourSide
assignments.value: We are the customer buying software services. The other party is the supplier.

assignments.name: playbook
assignments.value: Liability: supplier's cap should be at least 12 months of fees; we do not accept a cap below the annual contract value. Indemnity: supplier indemnifies us for IP infringement and data breaches caused by them. Termination: we can terminate for convenience with 30 days notice. Payment: net 30 from a correct invoice, no auto-escalation above 5% per year. Data: we own our data, it is returned on exit in a usable format, sub-processors are disclosed. IP: anything built specifically for us belongs to us. Confidentiality: mutual, surviving 3 years.

assignments.name: hardLimits
assignments.value: Supplier claims ownership of our data or of work built specifically for us. Unlimited liability on our side. No termination right for us at any point. Automatic renewal with no notice window. Governing law outside the EU or the UK.

assignments.name: extractionSystemPrompt
assignments.value:
You extract clauses from a contract. You do NOT judge them — a later step does that.

Read the document and return ONLY a JSON object, no markdown fences and no other text:

{
  "contract_type": string or null,
  "parties": [string],
  "governing_law": string or null,
  "effective_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" or null,
  "term_description": string or null,
  "clauses": [
    {
      "clause_id": string,
      "heading": string,
      "topic": string,
      "summary": string,
      "verbatim_key_sentence": string
    }
  ],
  "extraction_notes": string
}

Rules:
- `topic` should be a short normalised label such as: liability, indemnity, termination, payment, confidentiality, ip_ownership, data_protection, warranty, sla, non_compete, assignment, dispute_resolution, other.
- `verbatim_key_sentence` must be copied exactly from the document — it is what a lawyer will check against the original. Never paraphrase it.
- If a field is not present in the document, use null. Never guess a date, a party name, or a governing law.
- If this does not look like a contract, return an empty clauses array and explain why in extraction_notes.

nodes.name: Post Extraction to Anthropic API
nodes.notes: Raw call to the Messages API — needs an HTTP Header Auth credential with x-api-key set to your Anthropic key. Long timeout because a full contract takes a while to read.

nodes.name: Process Extracted Clauses
nodes.notes: Emits one item per clause. Throws deliberately if nothing was extracted — an empty review is worse than a failed one.

nodes.name: Batch Process Clauses
nodes.notes: Output 0 = done, output 1 = loop. 'Aggregate Clause Findings' is on the done output deliberately — it sums up every clause after the loop finishes. Some validators flag this as a mistake; it is not.

nodes.name: Collate Clause Findings
nodes.notes: Runs ONCE, on the loop's done output, with every assessed clause arriving as a separate item. This is the only node with the whole picture, which is why the verdict is computed here in plain code rather than by a model: a breached hard limit governs regardless of per-clause severity.

nodes.name: Notify via Review Channel
nodes.notes: Carries the three decision links. No-op if notifyWebhookUrl is blank.

nodes.name: Pause for Reviewer Input
nodes.notes: Pauses until Proceed / Redline / Reject is clicked.
